extraction.name: ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge
extraction.description: A new question set, text corpus, and baselines assembled to encourage AI research in advanced question answering. The ARC Dataset consists of a collection of 7787 natural science questions authored for use on standardized tests, partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set.
extraction.creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset consists of 7787 science questions drawn from a variety of sources through several months of extensive search and investigation. The ARC Corpus was created by utilizing a major search engine to run a large series of search queries relevant to science.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions are drawn from a variety of sources including standardized tests from various states and organizations (e.g., ACTAAP, AIMS, Alaska Dept Ed, CA Stnds Test, etc.) and an anonymous content partner (Mercury). The ARC Corpus was mined from the Web and augmented with the AristoMini corpus.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was partitioned into a Challenge Set (2590 questions), containing questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurrence algorithm, and an Easy Set (5197 questions), containing the remainder.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the ARC Corpus, the content of collected documents was stripped down to capture just the text, then chunked into sentences. For entailment computation, long sentences (>300 characters), sentences with negation, and noisy sentences were filtered from the retrieved sentences.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: To encourage AI research in advanced question answering. The dataset is partitioned into Train, Dev, and Test sets for training and evaluating question answering models.
